label: app:core
asserts: the diff touches apps/core/ or shared/. Derived from the diff and recomputed every push; it names no build because it is kept true by recomputation rather than by dating

label: app:plp
asserts: the diff touches apps/plp/ or shared/

label: app:pdp
asserts: the diff touches apps/pdp/ or shared/

label: app:checkout
asserts: the diff touches apps/checkout/ or shared/

label: app:mock
asserts: the diff touches external/ stand-ins. Lives in the app:* namespace for routing and is NOT a deployable of ours, which is the conflation that namespace turned out to carry

label: itil:standard
asserts: this change is a standard change: the diff is limited to pre-authorized paths. Derived. At most one itil:* may stand

label: itil:normal
asserts: this change is a normal change: it touches router/, gates/, change/, targets/ or .github/ and needs a human approval

label: itil:emergency
asserts: THIS change is the remedy, so it passes the freeze and the queue. Declared, never derived. Not the estate being shut

label: control-plane
asserts: this change alters how every FUTURE change is verified, so it cannot be verified by the pipeline it changes. Narrower than itil:normal, and the soak trigger

label: labeler:skip
asserts: the manifest is handed back to a human. Converts app:* from derived to asserted and says so where a reviewer can see it

label: change:requested
asserts: start my change request. The only label a person adds to set a change going; the pipeline clears it

label: change:scheduled
asserts: a window is booked. An entitlement to the path to production, not permission to deploy

label: change:complete
asserts: the change RECORD is closed passed. Terminal, persistent, and about the change rather than about any build

label: change:failed
asserts: ITIL closure code: the change did not complete. Production never served it, or served it and never made it live

label: change:backed-out
asserts: ITIL closure code: production DID serve this and was returned. Refused without --to <sha>, because the word asserts an estate action

label: change:backfill-owed
asserts: this change reached main without the normal evidence and still owes the window, the observations and the why. Blocks nothing. Persistent, because the merge is when the debt STARTS

label: deploy:staging
asserts: ACTION IN FLIGHT: a deployment to staging is running, and this is the berth claim guard 1 reads. Not a request and not a result

label: deploy:production
asserts: ACTION IN FLIGHT: a deployment to production is running. deploy-production.yml fires on it, so leaving it set leaves a dead change armed to re-enter production

label: release:start
asserts: the release has BEGUN for the booked change request. Never written by hand: adding it claims a deployment is running, which a person cannot truthfully assert

label: release
asserts: a person wants the release to go. The scheduler consumes it; a trigger that stays on re-fires

label: staging:e2e
asserts: the e2e instrument observed the journeys hold on staging. The LABEL cannot say on what build; the record can, which is why guard 4 authorizes on the record

label: staging:e2e-failed
asserts: the e2e instrument observed a failure on staging. Present alongside its pass it is a contradiction, not a pass

label: staging:smoke
asserts: the smoke instrument observed that a browser can use staging

label: staging:smoke-failed
asserts: the smoke instrument observed a failure

label: staging:uat
asserts: a person used the site on this build and accepted it. THE EXCEPTION: for acceptance the person IS the instrument. Not repeatable, so the label is durable and the record still names the build

label: staging:in-progress
asserts: action in flight

label: production:e2e
asserts: the e2e instrument observed the journeys hold in production

label: production:e2e-failed
asserts: the e2e instrument observed a failure in production

label: production:smoke
asserts: the smoke instrument observed production usable

label: production:smoke-failed
asserts: the smoke instrument observed a failure

label: production:healthy
asserts: the estate was SAMPLED N times per route and every sample carried the expected build. Sampled, never attested: nothing enumerated the instances

label: blocked:queue
asserts: guard 1 refused: another open PR holds the berth. The refusal, with its cause, standing where a reader can see it

label: blocked:lock
asserts: guard 3 refused: another deployment holds the deployment lock

label: blocked:freeze
asserts: guard 3 refused: a freeze or an emergency covers the requested window

label: blocked:diverged
asserts: guard 4b refused: main moved under this change. A human may clear it after rebasing, which is the one blocked:* a person may remove

label: freeze
asserts: ESTATE STATE: ordinary change is suspended. A property of the WORLD, carried on the estate holder issue, blocking everyone including its declarer

label: emergency
asserts: ESTATE STATE: an emergency is in flight out there. Grants NO exemption to whatever carries it, which is the whole reason it is not itil:emergency

label: hold:staging
asserts: REJECTED SEMANTICS. Still read, so a leftover stops a deploy rather than being silently ignored; its job is covered by freeze and by simply not approving

label: staging:passed
asserts: RETIRED. It named no measurement and no environment, so it could be satisfied by observing something else. Replaced by the staging:* stack plus records

label: staging:failed
asserts: RETIRED, same reason

label: deployed:production
asserts: RETIRED. Replaced by change:complete plus the deployment record

label: review:proxy
asserts: consent by a delegated proxy, backed by a record naming the SHA that was read. Never APPROVED, and the record says PROXY so nobody reads one as the other
